extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications providers, legal counsel, and stakeholders subject to the TCPA (e.g., ringless-voicemail vendors, robocall compliance officers, consumer advocates)
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive and enforcement standards governing whether 'ringless voicemail' is a 'call' under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act and therefore subject to consent and other TCPA requirements. Applies to providers of ringless voicemail and other internet-to-phone messaging services and to regulators/litigants assessing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ringless voicemail constitutes a 'call' under the TCPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission finds that 'ringless voicemail' to wireless phones is a 'call' made using an artificial or prerecorded voice and is therefore covered by the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The finding rests on functional/technical equivalence to previously-litigated internet-to-phone text messages and the ordinary meaning of 'call.' Because ringless voicemail directs messages using a consumer's wireless telephone number and depends on transmission of a voicemail notification alert to the consumer's phone, it meets the definition of a telephone call for TCPA purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer consent required for ringless voicemail to wireless numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Because ringless voicemail is a 'call' using an artificial or prerecorded voice to a wireless phone, it requires consumer consent under the TCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission denied All About the Message's request to declare ringless voicemail not subject to the TCPA and denied a retroactive waiver; providers may continue to offer the service only in compliance with the TCPA (i.e., with appropriate consent where required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of wireless telephone number is a necessary and unique identifier triggering TCPA coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Addressing a message using the consumer's wireless telephone number satisfies the TCPA requirement that the call be 'to any telephone number assigned to a [wireless] service.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission analogized ringless voicemail to internet-to-phone text messaging: when a caller or service uses the consumer's wireless telephone number (entered on a web portal, in an email string, etc.), the equipment effectively dials a telephone number assigned to a wireless service and thus makes a telephone call for purposes of section 227(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional equivalence / anti-form-over-substance principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Technological or procedural differences (e.g., adding an extra step or using internet delivery) that produce the same effect for the recipient do not remove TCPA protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission emphasized that from the recipient's perspective, internet-originated messages that function like phone-originated calls/texts cause identical harm; permitting differences in form would 'elevate form over substance' and could thwart Congressional intent to protect consumers as technologies evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary meaning of 'call' informs TCPA scope when statute is silent
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the TCPA does not define 'call,' courts and the Commission may consult ordinary dictionary definitions (e.g., Webster's) and legislative purpose to determine whether a communication is a 'call.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission cited Webster's definition 'to communicate with or try to get into communication with a person by a telephone' and found that ringless voicemail meets that ordinary meaning by directing messages via a wireless phone number and triggering voicemail retrieval by the consumer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-harm factors supporting coverage: intrusiveness, inability to block, voicemail impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission considered harms such as consumers' inability to block ringless voicemails, intrusion on time and privacy, possible brief ringing, and voicemail boxes filling with unwanted messages that can prevent wanted messages from being received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practical harms weighed against treating ringless voicemail as outside the TCPA; the Commission rejected arguments that ringless voicemail is non-invasive and used these harms as part of the policy rationale for requiring consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver standard for Commission rules: special circumstances/public interest required
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a waiver of the Commission's TCPA rules must demonstrate special circumstances or that granting the waiver is in the public interest; AATM did not meet that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission concluded it should not undermine statutory protections against robocalls by granting a waiver absent demonstration of special circumstances; AATM remains free to use ringless voicemail only in compliance with the TCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent that internet-to-phone texts initiated with an autodialer are 'calls' under the TCPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission previously held that computer-generated text messages sent to a carrier's server and routed to consumers are 'calls' for TCPA purposes when initiated with an autodialer, and reiterated that internet-to-phone text messaging is encompassed by the TCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This precedent was relied upon in finding ringless voicemail to be a call; the reasoning includes that the equipment dials a telephone number and the message is addressed to a number assigned to wireless service, producing the same effect on recipients as phone-originated texts/calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/engineering analogy: ringless voicemail delivery model parallels mass texting
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts described the technological steps and software delivery model for ringless voicemail as substantially the same as those used to deliver mass text messages to cellular subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission noted that neither AATM nor commenters disputed this technical description, and used the analogy to support the conclusion that ringless voicemail should be treated like other internet-originated communications already found to be 'calls' under the TCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCPA contains unique protections for wireless consumers that should not be undermined
rubrics_metrics.description: The TCPA provides 'unique protections' for wireless consumers which the Commission is unwilling to weaken absent compelling reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating petitions and waiver requests, the Commission weighs the statute's consumer-protection goals and is reluctant to find exemptions that would erode protections against unwanted robocalls and texts to wireless devices.
